Remedy: train only on quality-96 images in both classes and restrict real images to the generators' size window; cross-generator accuracy +11.06 points for ResNet-50 and +11.74 for Swin-T (Table 4).
Size as label. A detector for a 128-pixel generator misclassifies real images with a side of 100 to 150 pixels (Grommelt et al., Figure 3).

Resize direction as label. A leading detector 'associates downsampling with real images and upsampling with fake images' (Rajan et al., arXiv 2410.11835, Figure 2 caption). Remedy: make each fake by passing a real image through the generator's autoencoder only, at its own size; the aligned detector stays flat across the resize range and the set is 10 times cheaper to build. This is the published counterpart of our shrink-and-enlarge result.

Post-processing of one class learned as that class. Real training images were WEBP-compressed and the detector learned WEBP = real (Rajan and Lee, Stay-Positive, ICML 2025, arXiv 2502.07778, Section 3.1). Remedy: retrain the last layer with non-negative weights. The paper states its own limit: fake-associated patterns can also be spurious, and upsampled real images are still classified as fake (Section 6).

Pixel alignment still leaks through a frequency band. A reconstruction restores high-frequency detail that JPEG removed from the real image; a frequency-based detector flags about 93% of such reconstructions and detection collapses when a few high-frequency coefficients are masked (Chen et al., arXiv 2505.14359, Figures 4 and 5). Remedy: apply the real image's own JPEG quality to its reconstruction. Same mechanism as our softness floor (0.52 times Laplacian variance), opposite sign. The paper's introduction says 'high-frequency fusion' while the method as read describes matched compression; check the PDF.

Content and source as label. The same generated images are called real or fake by three CLIP-based detectors depending on the real photo collection they are paired with (B-Free, arXiv 2412.17671, Figure 2). Remedy: self-conditioned reconstruction plus inpainted variants; content alignment alone lifts balanced accuracy from 61.9 to about 81 (Table 2).

Preprocessing parity. Small mismatches in interpolation, initial size or file format between classes give near-perfect average precision that is only a formatting difference (Chai et al., ECCV 2020, arXiv 2008.10588, Table 5). Remedy: pass real images through the generator's own data transform, save both classes losslessly, resize both the same way. SAFE (Li et al., KDD 2025, arXiv 2408.06741) replaces resizing by cropping in training.

For whole generated faces the decisive patches are hair and background, and artefacts in flat background are the easiest for a generator to hide (Chai et al., Section 4.2 and the fine-tuned generator experiment). This is the counterpart of our border and backdrop cue.

Evaluation with matched real images. FakeInversion builds its test set by reverse image search so real and fake share style and theme (Cazenavette et al., CVPR 2024, arXiv 2406.08603); DDA-COCO pairs each real image with compression-aligned reconstructions from six autoencoders (Chen et al.). In morph detection the closest precedent is Zhang et al. (CVPRW 2024, arXiv 2501.09817), who put GAN-reconstructed genuine images in the genuine class of GAN morph sets; no radius-matched or history-crossed design was found.

In-the-wild drop. Open-source image detectors lose 45% of their AUC on Deepfake-Eval-2024 against earlier benchmarks (Chandra et al., arXiv 2503.02857, abstract); accuracy on scraped StyleGAN faces falls from 83.6 to 74.9% after resizing (Wang et al., arXiv 1912.11035).

ideas.name: Radius-crossed generator ladder: remove averageness by design, measure what is left
ideas.source_technique: Aligned training sets where the nuisance is equal in both classes (Rajan et al., ICLR 2025, arXiv 2410.11835; B-Free, Guillaro et al., CVPR 2025, arXiv 2412.17671; Dual Data Alignment, Chen et al., arXiv 2505.14359), distribution-matched latent operations (Agustsson et al., ICLR 2019, arXiv 1711.01970) and the Gaussianised StyleGAN latent space (Zhu et al., arXiv 2012.09036; Wulff and Torralba, arXiv 2009.06529).
ideas.transfer: Our spread-matched render equalises latent radius on the negative side only. Add the missing corner: the midpoint pushed back to full radius, G(centre + (m - centre)/s), decode only. Four arms result: single code at full radius, single code at the morph's radius, midpoint, midpoint at full radius; the label is 'two codes were mixed' and radius carries no label information. Build the same four arms from mapping-network samples, where supply is unlimited and no inversion is involved. Step 0 needs no image: since a render is a function of its code, no image detector can beat the best test on the exact code, so fit a cross-validated model on per-code summaries (radius per layer, spread across layers, skewness and excess kurtosis in the Gaussianised space) for midpoints against radius-matched single codes. All arms must use the same centre, the mean of that set's own codes: the existing control may shrink toward the generator's mean code, which would by itself explain part of the 0.58 to 0.63. Train the standard recipe on mixed against single; whatever it learns is a trace of linear mixing, not averageness. It decides how generator cells are reported and whether a generator arm belongs in training; it adds only same-generator images, so it cannot hurt landmark cells.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Both classes are outputs of one generator in one frame and file path, so generator fingerprint, storage history, border and capture detail are equal; the same persons feed both classes, so identity pool and expression are equal; radius is crossed, so averageness is equal. Shown by: two-person morph against spread-matched render (x3 vs x1s) and restored midpoint against one-photo reconstruction (x3r vs x1). The radius contrast x1s vs x1 must be separable by a radius probe (power) and not by the mixing head.
ideas.used_in_morph_detection_already: None found. Nearest: Zhang et al., CVPRW 2024 (arXiv 2501.09817) use GAN-reconstructed genuine images, with no radius control. Searches run: 'morphing attack detection StyleGAN latent space truncation averageness one-identity render control'; 'detect interpolated latent code GAN truncation classifier'; 'morphing attack detection kurtosis non-Gaussianity higher-order statistics'.
ideas.first_test: Step 0 on the stored W+ codes of the 423 StyleGAN3 pairs and the 64 GAN blocks, under an hour on CPU. Kill: code-level AUC at or below 0.60 with upper bound below 0.65; then print the limit and stop. If 0.75 or more: decode the restored midpoints for the 423 pairs and 4 x 2,000 prior-sample renders, run the FZ1 probe protocol plus one LoRA fine-tune. Positive control: radius contrast at or above 0.90. Pass: mixed against single at or above 0.70 in both radius strata on held-out codes. Kill: at or below 0.60 in both strata with the positive control passing.
ideas.risk: A high code-level AUC does not show that the image carries the trace; only the low outcome is decisive at step 0, and optimised codes are far from Gaussian, so step 0 may come out high while the image test ends in the kill. Restored midpoints of inverted codes may leave the generator's good region and show artefacts read as mixing (the prior-sample arm guards against this). A positive result reads 'two codes were mixed', which is also true of a same-person mix, not 'a second identity'.

ideas.name: Truncation-dose training: a pseudo-morph with no morph and no partner
ideas.source_technique: The truncation trick and its measured effect on samples (Karras et al. 2019, arXiv 1812.04948; Kynkaanniemi et al. 2019, arXiv 1904.06991), training on simulated traces instead of real fakes (Zhang, Karaman and Chang, WIFS 2019, arXiv 1907.06515) and real-only training (Liu et al., ECCV 2022).
ideas.transfer: A truncated render is one person morphed with the mean face. It has the one property a latent-average morph has and nothing else: no second person, no partner pool, no morphing tool. Train a head to regress the truncation factor on one-identity renders only and test it on real latent morphs. If the second-order picture is right, transfer is complete and the head has a physical unit, the mixing-equivalent truncation (0.71 unrelated, 0.87 look-alike, 1.0 single code). As evidence it shows constructively what 'detecting GAN morphs' reads. As a training arm it gives dose-labelled images at any scale from one photo per person, which removes the five-partner defect of SMDD for the generator arm. Under the opposite ruling the same renders enter training as genuine at several truncation levels and make the network blind to averageness. Alone it will not reach the published generator rows, which are won by reading the generator; it supplies the morph evidence under the policy 'a reconstruction is genuine' as an auxiliary target of the one network.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Both ends of the dose axis are renders of one generator through one file path, so storage history, border, capture detail, generator fingerprint and partner identity cannot differ. Shown by: camera photo against its history-matched copy must not move (at most 0.3 SD); two-person morph against spread-matched render must stay near 0.5 (declared unable to tell mixing from truncation); dose order trunc50 above trunc70 above plain renders. AUC reported as excess over the seven simple statistics, because truncated renders already differ in simple image properties at 0.96.
ideas.used_in_morph_detection_already: None found. SelfMAD makes pseudo-morphs by pixel blending; this has no blend. Searches run: 'face morphing attack truncation StyleGAN mean face pseudo-morph training'; 'morphing attack detection StyleGAN latent space truncation averageness'.
ideas.first_test: All images exist (trunc50, trunc70, re-decoded and spread-matched pools, 423 StyleGAN3 morphs). Fit the FZ1 probe on trunc70 against plain renders, folds by person, then score morphs against one-identity renders. Pass: AUC at or above 0.85 (the morph-trained probe reaches 0.89 to 0.94). Kill: below 0.75. Under an hour on cached or quickly extracted features.
ideas.risk: The head may read simple image properties rather than facial averageness. The existing truncated pools may use other base codes, layers or another centre than assumed; check the generation record. Behaviour on camera photos is untested. An attacker restores the radius (spherical interpolation is already used in MLSD-GAN, arXiv 2404.12679). Average-looking or beautified genuine faces would be flagged.

ideas.name: A declared 're-synthesised' output built by the aligned-pair recipe (improves the admissibility question already on our table)
ideas.source_technique: Fakes made by reconstructing real images (Rajan et al., arXiv 2410.11835; B-Free, arXiv 2412.17671), compression alignment of each pair (Chen et al., arXiv 2505.14359), crops instead of resizing (Li et al., KDD 2025, arXiv 2408.06741), end-to-end training rather than a frozen probe (B-Free, Table 3).
ideas.transfer: One network with three outputs: genuine, single-subject manipulation, morphing attack. The middle class is trained on same-photo pairs: a camera photo and its own one-photo reconstruction by StyleGAN inversion and by the diffusion autoencoder at each step count. Both members of a pair must share frame, size and file path; a pair that cannot be aligned without new resampling code is not used. The morph output is trained on morphs against reconstructions and same-person mixes. Error rates under both class policies come from one network: p(morph) alone, or 1 - p(genuine). A one-photo reconstruction is never called a morph. Under the policy 're-synthesised is inadmissible' this is the route to the published generator rows; under the other policy it changes no table number and still reports the class.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: Each pair shares content, person, expression and, after alignment, storage history and border; only the generator step differs for the middle class and only the mixing step for the morph class. Shown by: camera photo against history-matched copy must move neither output (at most 0.3 SD; flag rate at the 5% threshold at most 10%); reconstruction against camera photo (x1 vs x0) must move only the middle output; morph against reconstruction (x3 vs x1) only the morph output.
ideas.used_in_morph_detection_already: Partly. Zhang et al., CVPRW 2024 (arXiv 2501.09817) put GAN reconstructions in the genuine class; Colbois and Marcel, BIOSIG 2022 (arXiv 2209.00404) show a generated-image detector wins three GAN morph sets. A three-way output with a same-photo aligned middle class was not found.
ideas.first_test: Train the middle output on the 256 reconstruction pairs of the GAN blocks and the diffusion-autoencoder reconstructions on hand, folds by person. Pass: reconstruction against frame-matched camera photo at or above 0.95 on held-out persons with the history controls passing. Kill: history shift above 0.3 SD or flag rate above 10% after frame and compression alignment.
ideas.risk: Our first-pass 0.98 for reconstruction against camera photo includes frame, background and resolution changes and may fall after alignment. Each alignment tends to expose the next cue. Transfer to an unseen generator is weak in the source field (9.59% and 25.87% accuracy on a generator with a different autoencoder; Rajan et al., limitations).

ideas.name: Morph-free mechanism readers from the GAN field as independent instruments
ideas.source_technique: Released generated-image detectors that each read one known mechanism and never saw a morph: the ProGAN-trained classifier (Wang et al., CVPR 2020, arXiv 1912.11035; generator traces), NPR (Tan et al., CVPR 2024, arXiv 2312.10461; differences inside 2 x 2 pixel blocks, the trace of up-sampling) and DNA-Det (Yang et al., AAAI 2022, arXiv 2202.13843; pretrained on 170 image transformations).
ideas.transfer: Score our benchmark cells and every ladder rung with these readers, unchanged. A cell that a mechanism reader separates is separable by that mechanism. This is evidence for the shortcut claim from networks that are not ours and were trained on no morph. Expected pattern: the up-sampling reader moves with the storage-history step and with landmark cells whose morphs were stored small; the generator reader wins the GAN cells; none moves between a same-person and a two-person morph. The readers then serve as a control for our own network: its score should be unrelated to each reader's score within a class. It raises no table number; it strengthens the audit half of the paper.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: These are instruments, not our detector, so the one-network rule is untouched. They cannot have learned any cue of a morph benchmark, any partner identity or any morph tool. Shown by: photo against its history-matched copy (storage history), reconstruction against photo (generator), two-person against same-person morph (must stay near 0.5).
ideas.used_in_morph_detection_already: For GAN morphs with the ProGAN-trained classifier: yes (Colbois and Marcel, BIOSIG 2022, arXiv 2209.00404, EER 0.00 / 0.56 / 0.00%). DNADet features with a trained probe: yes (Colbois and Marcel, IJCB 2024, arXiv 2410.16802). An up-sampling reader on landmark cells, or any such reader on a matched ladder: none found (search: 'synthetic image detector zero-shot applied to face morphing attack detection landmark morphs NPR UnivFD').
ideas.first_test: Half a day: download the released weights, score the FRLL landmark cells, the MIPGAN cells, MorDIFF and the ladder rungs. Useful if the up-sampling reader reaches AUC at or above 0.90 on at least one landmark cell, separates a photo from its history-matched copy at or above 0.80, and stays at or below 0.60 between same-person and two-person morphs. Kill for the new part: below 0.75 on every landmark cell and below 0.70 on the storage-history step.
ideas.risk: NPR was trained on four ProGAN object classes at fixed size; behaviour on our frames is unknown. That NPR's weights are public is from memory. A negative outcome proves nothing about the cells. Licence terms must be read first.

ideas.name: Inversion-encoder bottleneck: read identity typicality where storage history cannot reach (improves identity shrinkage)
ideas.source_technique: Inversion-based tests (Karras et al. 2020, arXiv 1912.04958, Section 5; Albright and McCloskey, CVPRW 2019, arXiv 1905.02259), inversion plus biometric traits for synthetic faces (Pasquini et al., Applied Sciences 2023), encoders that keep codes near W (Tov et al. 2021, arXiv 2102.02766) and the Mahalanobis radius in the Gaussianised latent space (Zhu et al., arXiv 2012.09036).
ideas.transfer: The field asks whether the generator can reproduce the image. We ask where the image lands in the generator's code space. The detector is one inversion encoder; the decision is a fixed formula on its output: the Mahalanobis radius, in the Gaussianised space, of the coarse and middle layers only. Those layers carry pose, face shape and facial features; colour, microstructure and what a file history changes go to the fine layers and are discarded by construction. Landmark, latent and diffusion morphs should all land nearer the mean in the identity layers. The radius is measured from the mean code of inverted camera photos, not from the generator's mean code. The same quantity can be an auxiliary regression target for the main network at training time, so test time still uses one network. It is a component, not a headline: it does not by itself reach the published rows.
ideas.why_shortcut_free: The coarse and middle layer code cannot represent file format, file size, border or fine softness. Shown by: photo against history-matched copy (R0 vs R1) and photo against warp-only image (R0 vs R2w) must stay within 0.3 SD; two-person morph against its own warped halves and against the same-person morph (R4 vs R2w, R4 vs R3) carries the claim; graded-mixing rungs must rise with dose.
ideas.used_in_morph_detection_already: None found as a single-image detector. StyleGAN latent spaces are used for making morphs and for differential demorphing (SFDemorpher, arXiv 2603.28322). Searches run: 'morphing attack detection GAN inversion latent code encoder StyleGAN detect morph single image'; 'single image morphing attack detection StyleGAN encoder latent code Mahalanobis typicality inversion pSp e4e'.
ideas.first_test: The e4e encoder with StyleGAN2 is on disk from the MIPGAN controls (experiment AG1). Run it unchanged on the landmark ladder rungs of 300 hosts and the graded-mixing set. Pass: two-person morph against own warped halves at or above 0.75, history shift at most 0.3 SD, dose trend positive with an interval excluding zero. Kill: AUC below 0.65 or history shift above 0.3 SD.
ideas.risk: Ceiling is averageness of shape (0.725 on exact landmarks). The encoder may push blur into the middle layers; its input size and layer sources are from memory and must be checked in the code on disk. Images must reach the encoder's frame with the existing alignment only. A radius-restoring attacker defeats it for generator morphs.

does_not_transfer: Spectral and up-sampling detectors, fingerprints and attribution: a morph and a one-person render of the same generator carry the same trace; against camera photos the trace is exactly the cue we must exclude; it is also fragile (Chandrasegaran et al., CVPR 2021; Dong et al., CVPR 2022) and StyleGAN3 was designed without aliasing.

'Can the generator reproduce it' tests (projection into W, DIRE, AEROBLADE): the answer is yes for the morph and for the control; a midpoint lies in the region the generator renders well (2.4% of paths leave it; Kynkaanniemi et al. 2019).

One-class coding-cost and noise models (ZED, LNP): they measure how predictable the pixels are, and blending and softening both make pixels more predictable; in our record PNG size alone reaches 0.80 on one contrast. They would formalise the softness cue.

Stay-Positive: it stops features from voting for the genuine class, but our failure is a spurious feature voting for the morph class; the paper itself notes upsampled real images are still classified as fake.

Blur and JPEG augmentation (Wang et al. 2020): barred by our image-operation rule, and it hides small edits (face-aware liquify detected at chance; DeepFake average precision 98.2 to 89.0 with augmentation).
Frozen features as protection (UnivFD): refuted in our record and in the field's (resize-direction dependence, Rajan et al. Table 5; linear probe 68.5% against 95.2% end-to-end, B-Free Table 3).

Patch-only detectors: they remove global content cues such as expression but concentrate on local texture, where softness and storage history live; for generated faces the decisive patches are hair and background (Chai et al. 2020).
Thousands of generators in training (Park and Owens, CVPR 2025): the lesson transfers as 'diversity of partners and tools beats image count'; the scale does not fit three days.
Averageness as the detector for generator morphs: real but not specific (a truncated one-person render has it) and removable by the attacker with one multiplication.

The published generator-cell numbers as a target under the policy 'a reconstruction is genuine': they are reached by a network that never saw a morph, so a detector that ignores the generator cannot match them.

checks.field: Detection of diffusion-generated portraits (cross-field analysis for single-image morph detection)
references_wrong_or_unverifiable: Fast-DiM (Blasingame and Liu, arXiv 2310.09484), Table III: numbers 4.5 / 3.48 / 2.04 are right, but the reading built on them is not supported. The table is made by adding noise to a pixel-averaged morph and denoising under the averaged semantic code; it has no one-person row. It does not place 'the second person' in the stochastic code. Venue missing in the analysis: arXiv comment 'Accepted as a paper in IEEE Security and Privacy'.

Zhou et al., latent prior bias (arXiv 2506.00874), Table 1: 79.20 is the CLIP-plus-linear-head baseline, 94.63 is CLIP with LoRA rank 4 after adversarial training. The analysis prints both as 'CLIP with LoRA rank 4'.

B-Free (arXiv 2412.17671), Fig. 2: not 'the same DALL-E 3 fakes' against two real sets; the fakes are generated from RAISE or from COCO images and tested against reals of the same set. 'Always above 80%' is in the text of Appendix F; the figure number (Fig. 11) could not be confirmed.

DDA (arXiv 2505.14359): the paper says the detection rate 'drops dramatically' under high-frequency masking and gives no rate after masking, so 'removes the detection' is too strong. Venue now confirmed (arXiv comment 'NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight'). The frequency alignment is JPEG re-compression at the real image's estimated quality plus pixel mixing; 'fusion' is wording of the introduction only.

AEROBLADE (arXiv 2401.17879): the JPEG-against-PNG problem of DIRE's data is stated as a suspicion in the part I could read (Sec. 5.3, 'we suspect'); Sec. 9 was cut off by the page reader. 'Weaker than a trained detector under perturbation' holds against one detector only (Corvi et al.).
Cannas et al. (arXiv 2412.03261): numbers confirmed; venue 'ICCV Workshops 2025' is not shown on the arXiv page (v2, 18 Mar 2025). Not verified.
Zhang, Ramachandra, Raja, Busch (arXiv 2501.09817): quote confirmed; venue and pages (CVPR Workshops 2024, pp. 1510-1518) are not shown on the arXiv page. Not verified by me.
Staniszewski, Kucinski, Deja (arXiv 2410.23530): cited as 'v4 2025'; now v5 (27 Jan 2026) with arXiv comment 'ICLR 2026'. Numbers confirmed.

Diffusion Autoencoders (arXiv 2111.15640): SSIM 0.927 and 0.991 confirmed (CelebA-HQ at 128 px), but 'their Table 2' is unsure: the page reader places 0.991 (MSE 6.07e-5) in Table 1 and the step sweep in the ablation table. Check the PDF.

Rajan et al. (arXiv 2410.11835): the quoted sentence is the caption of Fig. 2 and is about one detector ('Corvi associates downsampling with real images ...'), not about unaligned training in general.
'Organic or Diffused' (Ha et al.) is listed as 'searched, not found'. It exists: arXiv 2402.03214.
Not re-opened in this check: the other 23 entries the analysis marks as found in search results only, and MAD-DDPM, FD-MAD, MADPromptS.
Limit: the shared web-search budget ran out after 8 searches (4 more refused). 'Not found' statements are bounded by that.
claims_corrected: 'The second person sits mostly in the stochastic code' and 'the field predicts the stochastic code' are not supported. Preechakul et al. (changing the noise map 'only affects minor details'), the DiM paper, and our own AD1b distances (semantic code 0.773 same person against 1.744 other person; noise maps 0.97 to 0.99 for everyone) say coarse identity is in the semantic code. Correct statement: open question; both codes are needed for face-recognition success.

Proposal 1's side instrument (render from the semantic code with fresh noise 'drops the contributors' identity') has no source. Such a render keeps coarse identity, so a detector that still separates a cell on it may read the averaged semantic code, which is morph evidence.
'Under our constraints this is the one permitted operation that changes low-level statistics' is false: the existing shrink-and-enlarge path, run unchanged, is permitted and does so.
Proposal 2's score s = log P(M) - log(P(G)+P(S)) is the log-odds of P(M) under a softmax. A binary head with the same negatives estimates the same quantity; only the training signal differs.

'None found in morph detection' for the same-person negative is wrong and contradicts our own 14_CLASS_DEFINITIONS.md. Confirmed in the paper: MorDeephy (arXiv 2208.03110, Sec. 4.3) 'we consider selfmorphs as bona fide samples'. Kashiani et al. (IJCB 2023) use same-person morphs as attacks.

'Published audit of dataset shortcuts: not found' needs an exception: Spreeuwers, Schils, Veldhuis (EUSIPCO 2018) report 80% and 79% EER across sets (Table II) and show that down-up scaling of morphs by 0.5 raises EER from about 5% to above 12%.

'Equal processing of both classes exists only as evaluation practice' is too narrow: Seibold et al. 2018 (noise and blur on both classes, Sec. 4.2) and Ferrara et al. (simulated print-and-scan on all training images) do it in training.
'The closest thing to our ladder is one matched step' should read 'no per-image ladder with matched controls': Semi-Truths has graded edits and FakeChain has chains of one to three manipulations.

Proposals 2 and 3 repeat ideas already in round 3 and vetted at 18:29 (ideas/round3/mechanism_ideas.md, Idea 1 three-level ordinal score and Idea 2 code-factorised twins). The analysis does not mention them.

Proposal 1: 'file size equal by construction' is wrong for lossless files (PNG size follows content: 0.877 for diffusion morph against photo in our record). The pass also does not equalise earlier history: Mandelli Table I separates two populations sharing one decoder at 0.994.

Proposal 3: 'the MorDIFF cell is then scored by mixing evidence' is not supported by the record: under the mix-trained head, diffusion morph against camera photo equals PNG size (0.876 against 0.877, unreviewed).

Proposal 3 statistics: two factors are tested, so the chance that at least one reaches 13 of 16 under no effect is about 0.021, not 0.011. The kill rule is one-sided although the record has 0.249 (a strong reversed signal).

Proposal 4: the cue-only AUC 'on every evaluation cell' will read 1.0 by our own reviewed finding (a file attribute separates the classes in all 17 cells). That line is the audit, not a certificate of the method.
Mandelli et al.: the pipeline is two detectors in sequence on 96 px patches (not one network), and the camera-model test is on the Vision set, not on faces.
Zhou et al. (arXiv 2509.12995): the pretraining-exposure explanation is worded by the authors as speculation.

ideas.name: Common last hop: pass both classes through the unchanged autoencoder (audit protocol and training crossing)
ideas.one_line: The training crossing already exists in the diffusion ladder, and the audit outcome is predicted by the 256 px output size that we already measured.
ideas.closest_prior_work_in_morph_detection: ReGenMorph (Damer et al., ISVC 2021, arXiv 2108.09130): a landmark morph re-generated through a StyleGAN encoder and generator; genuine images not re-generated; attack strength falls. Genuine side: one sentence in Zhang et al. (arXiv 2501.09817). Equal degradation of both classes in training: Seibold et al. (arXiv 1806.04265), Ferrara et al. (arXiv 1901.08811). Neighbouring field: Chai et al. (arXiv 2008.10588); Liu et al., 'Exploiting the Final Component' (arXiv 2601.20461). In our own files: x1 of the diffusion ladder is this pass, and the canonical-view front end of round3/nuisance_ideas.md does the same job with the approved shrink path.
ideas.likeliest_confound: Storage history in the form of output size. The pass returns a 256 px image; the SelfMAD release flags 45% of genuine photos after a 50% shrink-and-enlarge and 97% of photos stored small, so its separation collapses with no help from the decoder. Second: softness changed by the pass itself (SSIM 0.927 at 20 steps; sharper renders at 100 steps). Control: an aligner-only arm (the 256 px frame saved before encode and render) beside the pass at 20 and 100 steps, with Laplacian variance printed for every arm.
ideas.revised_first_test: Only if the lead wants one number; no new inversion. Hosts whose x0 and x1 exist at 20 and 100 steps (A43 or DG1). Save the aligner's 256 px frame for the same hosts (needs the lead's reading of the rules). Score the SelfMAD and MADation releases through their own crop path on four arms of the same genuine photos: raw, aligner only, pass at 20, pass at 100. If the aligner-only flag rate is within 10 points of the pass, the decoder adds nothing and the idea ends. Only a gain of 20 points or more over aligner-only is a new audit row, reported in the single-subject table.
ideas.reason: The decoder trace is already on both sides of the label (x1, x2 against x3) and on neither side in the landmark ladder, so laundering landmark rungs adds cost and no new contrast (SMDD would cost about 144 A100-hours). The pass does not remove earlier history (Mandelli Table I: 0.994 inside one decoder), may erase or invert softness, and a laundered morph needs a new face-recognition check (ReGenMorph lost attack strength). The diffusion-cell half of the audit is an established result. No table number rises.

ideas.name: One network with three outputs; the morph score is the contrast against both non-morph classes
ideas.one_line: Same idea as the round-3 three-level score with an unordered head; keep it only as one extra arm of the labelling comparison, decided by a LoRA fit.
ideas.closest_prior_work_in_morph_detection: In our own files: Idea 1 of round3/mechanism_ideas.md (three-level ordinal score), vetted to 'revise'. Published: MorDeephy (arXiv 2208.03110; same-person morphs merged into the genuine class of a binary detector); Seibold et al. (arXiv 1806.04265; multi-class pretraining by number of morphed regions); Di Domenico et al. (arXiv 2404.07667; three classes, differential setting). A single-image head with a separate single-subject class was not found (search budget limited).
ideas.likeliest_confound: Capture detail and geometry as source disparity: the two-person warp is larger than the same-person warp, so softening and the ghosted surround are stronger (background alone 0.54 to 0.59, thumbnail 0.62 to 0.65 for R4 against R3); on FRLL the second photo of the same person is the smiling one (1.43 times file size). Control: no FRLL pairs; R4 against R3 inside the overlapping band of landmark shape distance; the best simple-statistic floor printed beside it; a face-blanked read-out.
ideas.revised_first_test: One extra arm in the existing three-arm comparison, landmark family only, FRGC and colorFERET hosts, no generator rungs, same images in every arm: (i) binary, negatives genuine only; (ii) binary, negatives genuine plus single-subject; (iii) three-way softmax scored by the log-odds of P(M). Linear heads on cached features are a plumbing check; one LoRA fit per arm decides. Read: R4-against-R3 AUC inside the matched band as excess over the floor; share of R4 caught at the threshold that flags 5% of R3; shift from R0 to R1 and to R2w; EER on FRLL landmark cells. Kill arm (iii) if it does not beat arm (ii) by 0.03 AUC with a person-bootstrap interval excluding zero.
ideas.reason: With a softmax the score is the log-odds of P(M), which a binary head with the same negatives also estimates; the proposed CPU test compares only boundary shapes. Training genuine against single-subject teaches the pipeline and generator split that the paper criticises (SMDD genuine images are StyleGAN2 renders). Morph against single-subject is weak where clean (0.61 to 0.66 on GAN morphs; 0.249 on diffusion morphs), so many morphs are missed at a threshold that protects single-subject images. Its one advantage over the ordinal version: it does not force an order that the diffusion record violates. No table number rises.

ideas.name: Code-factorial rungs and footprint-matched, step-crossed pairs for diffusion-autoencoder morphs
ideas.one_line: Merge with the round-3 code-factorised twins; keep the second photo of the same person as the constant-footprint design; drop the training rule and the directional prediction.
ideas.closest_prior_work_in_morph_detection: Training rule: MorDeephy (arXiv 2208.03110) and its follow-ups label same-person morphs as genuine for landmark tools; Kashiani et al. (arXiv 2308.10392) label them as attacks. Rungs: attack papers only (DiM variants A to D, arXiv 2301.04218; Fast-DiM Table III, arXiv 2310.09484). In our own files: Idea 2 of round3/mechanism_ideas.md, vetted to 'revise' with a fresh-noise cell. A detection-side factorial was not found in the literature.
ideas.likeliest_confound: Capture detail as source disparity: a two-person pair is farther apart than a same-person pair (semantic code 1.744 against 0.773; hair, collar, pose, backdrop). 'B in the semantic code' may be 'codes farther apart'; 'B in the noise map' may be the ghost of another head outline (alignment and surround cue). Controls: semantic-code distance and landmark shape distance as covariates and the contrast inside the overlapping band; face-interior and surround-only read-outs by constant-colour blanking; Laplacian variance and PNG size of every cell (softness with reversed sign).
ideas.revised_first_test: Step 1, CPU, no render (PD1 diffusion features, 129 FERET and FRGC blocks; A43): rank correlation of the x3-against-x2 score with pair distance inside each class; AUC of x3 against x2 inside the overlapping distance band, both directions; the simple-statistic floor at 20 steps. Stop if the within-class correlation is 0.5 or more in absolute value or fewer than 30 pairs per class share a band. Step 2, only if Athena saves both codes: six cells per host at 20 steps for at least 200 hosts (four corners with A' or B in each code, a fresh-noise cell, the reconstruction), scored by a person-disjoint probe trained on morph against reconstruction. Pass: one factor has a paired effect whose 95% person-bootstrap interval excludes zero with the covariates included, and it holds in the face-interior read-out. Kill: both intervals include zero. The 16 AD1b persons are a plumbing run only.
ideas.reason: The real gain over the round-3 design is that both codes are mixed in every cell and only the partner changes. The rest needs repair: the prediction is not backed by the sources; the read-out is the unstable projection of the record (0.793 'not consistent', 0.249, 0.438); n = 16 with two factors; a one-sided kill rule; inverted codes of the existing material are not on disk. The training rule has no route to the published cell (0.876 against PNG size 0.877) and is not new for landmark morphs. Value is in what may be claimed on diffusion cells, not in a table number.

ideas.name: Alignment by selection, with a frequency-only certificate and paired batches (upgrade of the SMDD rebuild)
ideas.one_line: The only proposal that attaches a checkable statement to the reported network; use matching in place of weights, measure cues at the network's input size, and add a random-subsample control.
ideas.closest_prior_work_in_morph_detection: Equalising by processing both classes: Seibold et al. (arXiv 1806.04265), Ferrara et al. (arXiv 1901.08811), Zhang et al. (arXiv 2501.09817). Showing that a detector learnt the set: Spreeuwers et al. (EUSIPCO 2018). Selection of existing images until a cue-only classifier is at chance, printed as a property of the training set: not found in morph detection. Outside it: Grommelt et al. (arXiv 2403.17608), REPAIR (arXiv 1904.07911), AFLite (arXiv 2002.04108). In our own files: the certificate of the canonical-view idea and the round-1 reweighting idea.
ideas.likeliest_confound: Less data alone: a weaker head flags less of everything at a fixed threshold, which looks like a halved R0-to-R1 change. And a cue outside the vector takes over: the five fixed SMDD partners, or the generator and pipeline step (readable at 0.91 to 0.98 by features, invisible to eight spectrum bands). Softness is caused by blending (0.52 times), so balancing on it removes true evidence. Controls: a random subsample of equal size; thresholds re-set per arm at the same false-alarm rate on unprocessed genuine photos with the landmark miss rate printed; partner identity, pool and engine added as cues; a strong-reader check (frozen-feature probe and the morph-free network refitted on the matched pool).
ideas.revised_first_test: CPU, hours. Pool: SMDD rebuild arms plus the landmark ladder, FRLL excluded. Cues at the detector's input size: Laplacian variance at three kernel sizes, eight radial bands, border fraction, history flag, engine, pool, partner identity. Cue-only classifier with person-disjoint folds; build a matched subsample. Three logistic heads on cached CLIP features: full pool, matched subsample, random subsample of equal size. Read: cue-only AUC before and after; share of data kept; R0-to-R1 flag-rate change at each head's own 5% threshold; R4-against-R3 AUC; R4-against-R0 EER. Kill: cue-only AUC cannot reach 0.60 while keeping 30% of the pool; or the matched head does not beat the equal-size random subsample by at least half of the full-pool flag-rate change; or landmark EER worsens by more than 2 points against the random subsample. On a pass: one LoRA fit on the matched pool beside the round-2 arm.
ideas.reason: Cheap, needs no generator and no class ruling, and gives the paper a named-cue list with a number per cue, the claim form the field uses. Sample weights fade in deep networks (Byrd and Lipton, arXiv 1812.03372) and subsampling is the reliable form (Sagawa et al., arXiv 2005.04345; Idrissi et al., arXiv 2110.14503), so the weighting variant is replaced. The certificate covers named cues only and reads 1.0 on evaluation cells by construction of the benchmarks; the ladder stays the evidence there. It will not raise a table number and may cost some on landmark cells.
