Ref 34 Forensics Adapter: the arXiv record now carries the journal version (title 'Forensics Adapter: Unleashing CLIP for Generalizable Face Forgery Detection', comment 'TPAMI 2026'); the list gives the CVPR 2025 title. Cite one version, not a mix.
Ref 53 PW-MAD: per-pixel labels confirmed; that the target map is constant is not stated in the text I could read (plausible, not confirmed).
Ref 10 OST: only the abstract page was opened; the quoted Table 1 numbers were not re-checked.

Limit of the whole check: the session's shared web-search budget ran out after seven searches, so later verification used only pages with known addresses. All numbers were read through an automated page reader and need a PDF re-check before use.
claims_corrected: GenD Table 4: the analysis says all methods were 'retrained on the same data'. The paper says Effort (88.5) and Forensics Adapter (88.4) were scored with 'their officially released weights'; only GenD is trained by the authors, on FaceForensics++.
GenD supplement Table S7: true-positive rate at 1% false positives for GenD (CLIP) ranges from 10.9% (DSv2) to 92.9% (UADFV), mean 49.1%; the analysis gives 92.3% as the maximum.

DF40 does not use the same real data for all 40 methods: its Table 2 lists FaceForensics++ and Celeb-DF for most, but UADFV, VFHQ, FFHQ and CelebA for others. The StyleCLIP collapse (0.006) arises because the resolution relation between real and fake flips in such a domain. The finding and the quote are otherwise right.

'Same-person morph labelled genuine: yes, once (Pimenta et al.)' is wrong. MorDeephy (Medvedev, Shadmand, Goncalves, ICPRAM 2023, arXiv 2208.03110) did it first with about 500,000 same-person morphs ('we consider selfmorphs as bona fide samples'); Pimenta et al. is its follow-up and uses the same identity-based scheme (two networks, dot-product score), not just a binary label choice.

'Deepfake detectors scored on morphs: not found' is contradicted by the analysis's own reference 50: SelfMAD Table I scores SBI on morph sets (EER 11.76 / 13.73 / 12.25 / 44.61 / 39.22 on FRLL-Morphs AMSL / FaceMorpher / OpenCV / StyleGAN2 / WebMorph; average 27.55 over all test sets; page-reader values).

OrthoMAD is not simply 'trained on SMDD': it is trained separately on five sets (MorGAN-LMA, MorGAN-GAN, LMA-DRD digital and print-scan, SMDD) and has no identity supervision at all (binary cross-entropy plus an orthogonality penalty).

Caldeira et al. (EUSIPCO 2023): targets are autoencoder latents, not FR embeddings, and the decision score is 1 - id1*id2, a function of the two slots; this is closer to proposal 5.4 than the analysis states.

Proposal 5.4 says it upgrades 'the two-contributor embedding head already in our plan (T5)'. Our record says that head failed twice (demorph head S8; reference-free demorpher 0.00 to 0.27% strict recovery) and IDEAS_v1 section E drops it.

Proposal 5.3 says the audit use on released detectors and the gradient rule are new. Both are in ROUND1_raw.json ('Null-space surgery ... from our head and from the released MADation heads'; 'History-null constrained adaptation'; 'Counterfactual-pair erasure') and listed in PLANNING_RECORD section 14.1 as not taken. New are only the 'subspace only' read-out from S3 Figure 2b and S3 as a citation.

The pass mark 'R3 against R4 at least 0.85' (5.1, 5.2) does not test the ideas: the alpha-field head that fails its warp control already reaches 0.853, and warp size alone predicts R3 against R4 at 0.81 pooled and 0.92 on FERET (PLANNING_RECORD section 14.1).

The softness cross of 5.1 is not a cross: with weight 0.5 on the one-person part and 0.25 to 0.3 on the two-person part, the two-person part is always the sharper one, which plants a reverse cue. The weight field must be drawn independently of the identity field.
'5 folds by person' must hold out both persons of every morph; the record found that folds by host alone leak the partner (gate_c.py).
ED4 spatial-bias evidence is not only attention maps: Figure 8 (score change under crop, resize, shift) and Table VI are quantitative, though indirect.

S3: the abstract says the subspace is suppressed 'in feature representations' while the method projects gradients; the abstract claims 'multiple benchmarks' while all experiments use DF40; the best strength is given as 0.7 in one section and 0.5 in an appendix; Figure 2b has no numbers in the text.

SBI: colour and frequency changes go to source or target at random, resize and shift to the source only; the 69.11 result is on a 20,000-image set of FFHQ photos and StyleGAN renders, not on 20,000 StyleGAN faces.

ProDet: Table 2 averages three test sets and Table 1 four, so the two averages are not comparable; the module that turns the three attribute outputs into an attention map is not specified in the paper.

ideas.name: Second-identity field with a one-person blend as its complement
ideas.one_line: The only new construction of the four, but its softness cross plants a reverse cue, the partner's capture session is uncrossed, and no arm shows that the field beats a plain image label.
ideas.closest_prior_work_in_morph_detection: Seibold et al., J. Inf. Secur. Appl. 2020 (arXiv 1806.04265): partial morphs whose complement is the untouched photo, with a four-class region scheme. Also PW-MAD (arXiv 2108.10291, per-pixel labels) and Qin, Peng, Long, IEEE TIFS 2022 (DOI 10.1109/TIFS.2022.3212276, localises morphed regions; abstract level only, full text must be read before a novelty claim). Our own round-1 raw idea 'Region-partial morphs with patch-level mixing targets' uses the warped host as complement. No work found with a same-person blend as complement.
ideas.likeliest_confound: Capture detail: host and its second photo usually share session, lighting and hair, the partner does not, so the field can read 'second capture session' (ghost energy in hair, collar, lighting) instead of 'second person'. Second: mid-frequency cancellation (the band-power statistic that reaches 0.89 to 0.91 for warp-only against morph) differs between the parts and cannot be crossed. Control: cross session with person (one-person part from another session, partner from the same session as that photo, FRGC), blank the periphery with constant colour, draw the weight field independently of the identity field, and report within-image AUC as excess over the band-power statistic on the same patches.
ideas.revised_first_test: One day, CPU build plus cached DINOv3 tokens, ridge patch head, folds holding out both persons. Build 1,500 composites with independent identity and weight fields, 300 seam-only, 300 double-run uniform images each for field 0 and field 1, and 300 other-session composites where FRGC allows. Fit three heads on the same patches: (a) composite field, (b) image label broadcast (R3 = 0, R4 = 1), (c) the existing alpha-field head. Read on the OpenCV-style engine: R3 against R4 inside thirds of landmark displacement with periphery blanked; within-image AUC against the band-power statistic; shifts R0 to R2w and R0 to R1; double-run against single-run uniform scores. Pass: geometry-matched R3 against R4 at least 0.75 (lower bound above 0.65) and at least 0.05 above head (b); within-image AUC at least 0.05 above band power, also on other-session composites; R0 to R2w at most 0.3 SD; at most 10% of history-matched photos flagged. Kill: head (a) not better than (b) by 0.03 and no halving of the R2w shift; or other-session within-image AUC below 0.55; or geometry-matched R3 against R4 below 0.65; or R2w shift above 0.5 SD.
ideas.reason: Checked against the record: the alpha-field head already reaches R3 against R4 0.853 while failing the warp control (0.73 SD), so the stated pass mark is no test; composites are warped twice and uniform ladder rungs once, so double-run uniform cases are needed; the within-image contrast helps only in training and must beat an image-label arm. Needs two author rulings (double run of the wrapper, class of a composite), is silent on generator morphs, and reaches a trained network by 14 Nov only if day one passes.

ideas.name: Cumulative ladder code instead of one morph label
ideas.one_line: Keep one-person blends as negatives of the attack score, but test the multi-bit code against a plain binary label in an adapted network; the frozen-feature test proposed does not test the code.
ideas.closest_prior_work_in_morph_detection: MorDeephy (Medvedev, Shadmand, Goncalves, ICPRAM 2023, arXiv 2208.03110) and Pimenta et al. (arXiv 2309.00549): same-person morphs labelled genuine in training. SelfMAD (arXiv 2504.05504) and Kashiani et al. (IJCB 2023, arXiv 2308.10392) label them attack. No ordered multi-bit code found. On our own table: round-3 recipe 1 (ladder-ordered loss), whose review today says to drop the order term.
ideas.likeliest_confound: Softness driven by warp size, plus the alignment-independent outline ghost: geometry alone predicts same-person against two-person at 0.81 pooled and 0.92 on FERET, and same-person photos share hair and shoulders. For the mirror rung, left-right symmetry (asymmetry 2.1 against 12.0). Control: read the third bit inside geometry-matched groups, blank the periphery with constant colour in every rung, keep R3m out of the loss (test-only), report excess over landmark displacement, Laplacian variance and band power, hold out both persons, and require the soft dose label to stay flat on same-person graded mixes.
ideas.revised_first_test: CPU floor first (hours): logistic third bit on cached mean tokens, read geometry-matched and periphery-blanked; stop if R3 against R4 is below 0.65 or the excess over the best simple statistic is below 0.05. Then three small LoRA fits on the MADation recipe, same images and folds: arm A binary (R4 against R0, R1, R2w, R3), arm B cumulative three-bit code without the history bit, arm C one-hot classes. Read on persons held out as pairs, OpenCV-style engine: geometry-matched R3 against R4 with interval, shifts R0 to R1 and R0 to R2w, share of history-matched photos flagged, native EER on FRLL landmark cells. Pass for the code: B beats A by at least 0.03 on geometry-matched R3 against R4 or halves the R2w shift at no more than 1 point of EER, and is not worse than C. Otherwise use the binary label and cite ProDet and ED4 for the negatives.
ideas.reason: ProDet is verified and says what the analysis claims, but on frozen features three bits are three separate probes, so the first test only re-measures one-person negatives (already 0.759 in the paired-difference experiment). A supervised history bit asks the features to encode history, while our pair-trained heads already sit at the 5% flag floor. ProDet's aligned anchors do not exist for us and its attention module is unspecified. The third bit is trained on exactly the contrast that today's round-3 review warned forces a symmetry or outline-ghost separator.

ideas.name: History-subspace surgery: audit released detectors by projection, then keep gradients out of the subspace
ideas.one_line: Keep the audit as a half-day figure with random, placebo and blend-evidence controls; drop the gradient rule as a method, since data crossing already removes the cue.
ideas.closest_prior_work_in_morph_detection: None found for projection or erasure; nearest published neighbour is Kashiani et al., IJCB 2023 (arXiv 2308.10392, consistency across augmented views). The nearest work of all is our own ROUND1_raw.json, which already holds the audit on released MADation heads, the adaptation rule and the erasure variant. Outside morph detection the peer-reviewed forms are LEACE (arXiv 2306.03819), iterative null-space projection (arXiv 2004.07667) and the conditional variance penalty (arXiv 1710.11469).
ideas.likeliest_confound: Softness: a landmark morph is soft by physics (0.52 times the Laplacian variance) and storage history moves the same number, so the history subspace holds real blend evidence; a rise in benchmark error after removal then looks like 'the number rested on storage history'. Also no baseline: a random rank-16 subspace may do the same. Control: ladder R2w against R4 before and after removal (same history on both sides, so any loss is lost blend evidence); 100 random subspaces and the top principal directions of genuine features; a placebo subspace from lossless flip; estimate on one photo pool and read on another; report the cosine of the subspace with the benchmark class difference and with the ladder difference R4 minus R2w.
ideas.revised_first_test: Half a day, features and linear algebra only, on the MADation ViT-B/16 release and SelfMAD through their own preprocessing. Subspace from R1 minus R0 on pool A at rank 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. Score with full features, subspace removed, subspace only; repeat for random, principal-direction and flip subspaces. Read on pool B and the FRLL landmark cells: share of history-matched photos flagged at the fixed threshold, EER, ladder R2w against R4. Usable audit finding: at some rank of at most 16 the subspace-only EER stays within twice the full EER while the three baselines are near chance, and R2w against R4 loses at most 0.03 after removal. If R2w against R4 loses more than 0.10, report 'intrinsic collinearity' and use no projection in training. Kill: no rank lowers the flagged share on pool B by a quarter, or the baselines do as well.
ideas.reason: S3 is verified (single dataset, single runs, internal inconsistencies). For a linear head the audit adds only the 'subspace only' read-out to the image-level intervention we already have. The training rule has no room: a data-level chain already cut flags from 19 to 40% to 4 to 8% at 0.4 to 1.5 points (A30 amendment 6), our pair-trained heads flag 3.9 to 5.4% (the floor), and our consistency loss (A49) gave no gain. The ViT-L/14 release cannot be audited until the own-crop re-score reproduces published numbers.

ideas.name: Identity-agreement slots with a partner-retrieval test
ideas.one_line: Largely exists as MorDeephy, the head it upgrades failed twice in our record, and the retrieval falsifier is passed by any reader of the morph's mixed identity.
ideas.closest_prior_work_in_morph_detection: MorDeephy (Medvedev, Shadmand, Goncalves, ICPRAM 2023, arXiv 2208.03110): two identity embeddings trained on the two contributors' identity classes, single-image score is their dot product, about 500,000 same-person morphs labelled genuine; follow-ups arXiv 2309.00549, 2309.00665, 2402.14665 and MorphGuard (arXiv 2505.10497). Also Caldeira et al., EUSIPCO 2023 (arXiv 2306.03002, score 1 - id1*id2) and OrthoMAD (BIOSIG 2022, arXiv 2208.07841).
ideas.likeliest_confound: For the score: softness and ghost size driven by warp size (same-person sources have FR cosine 0.87, two-person 0.23; geometry alone gives 0.81 to 0.92). For the retrieval test: a morph matches both contributors by construction, and pairs are matched in sex and ethnicity, so a mixed-identity or demographics reader beats the stated 5% chance; with SMDD as released the five fixed partners can be memorised. Control: geometry-matched groups with periphery blanked; a sex- and ethnicity-matched gallery without the host; a baseline using the ArcFace embedding of the morph itself for both slots; a direction test in which the slot difference must align with the contributors' embedding difference more than with a random third person's.
ideas.revised_first_test: Only as a one-hour diagnostic for other heads, with no slot training. On held-out R4 images with existing ArcFace embeddings: (i) baseline, rank the true partner by the ArcFace embedding of the morph itself in a matched gallery of at least 100 held-out persons without the host; (ii) regress the penultimate features of the head under test onto the embedding difference host minus partner (ridge, both persons held out) and compare the cosine with the true difference against that with a random third person. Pass: direction cosine above the random-person value with lower bound above 0. A slot head is worth building only if it beats baseline (i) in partner rank.
ideas.reason: The Identity Consistency Transformer is verified (51.48 on Celeb-DF v2 without the consistency loss), but the transfer is not new and not feasible here. Our record: the two-contributor head failed twice and was dropped (reference-free demorpher 0.00 to 0.27% strict recovery), the identity ceiling for generator cells is estimated at 0.59 to 0.78, and a head on frozen tokens with about 430 persons cannot learn a map into FR space for new persons. It needs a many-partner training set and an adapted network that cannot be built and reviewed by 14 Nov. Keep MorDeephy as a related-work citation and the direction test as a diagnostic.

missed_by_the_analyst: Rebalanced Deepfake Detection Protocol: W.-H. Wang et al., 'In Anticipation of Perfect Deepfake: Identity-anchored Artifact-agnostic Detection under Rebalanced Deepfake Detection Protocol', arXiv 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.00483. Genuine videos re-created with the forgery tool from the same person are labelled genuine ('whitehat'), and the same processing (resize, JPEG, video compression, blur) is applied to both classes ('surrogate'). Table 1: Xception about 0.92 to about 0.61 under whitehat; non-identity baselines lose 18 to 35% on average. The deepfake field's version of our ladder and storage-history control; its own detector needs a reference video.

MorDeephy: I. Medvedev, F. Shadmand, N. Goncalves, 'MorDeephy: Face Morphing Detection Via Fused Classification', ICPRAM 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.03110. Two identity embeddings, dot-product score on a single image, about 500,000 same-person morphs labelled genuine. Closest prior work to proposal 5.4 and to the label choice of 5.2; already cited in our round-3 files. Follow-ups: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.00665, https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14665, https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10497.

SelfMAD's own Table I scores the deepfake detector SBI on morph benchmarks (https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05504): 12 to 14% EER on FRLL-Morphs landmark cells, about 40% on StyleGAN2 and WebMorph. This is the measured answer to 'what happens if the deepfake recipe is moved unchanged'.

L. Qin, F. Peng, M. Long, 'Face Morphing Attack Detection and Localization Based on Feature-Wise Supervision', IEEE TIFS 2022, DOI 10.1109/TIFS.2022.3212276 (abstract level only): its fine-grained loss locates morphed regions. Open question for the novelty of proposal 5.1; the full text has not been read in any round.

Peer-reviewed forms of what S3 does by heuristics: LEACE (Belrose et al., NeurIPS 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.03819); iterative null-space projection (Ravfogel et al., ACL 2020, https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.07667); conditional variance penalty over groups of the same object under a style change (Heinze-Deml and Meinshausen, https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.11469); last-layer retraining (Kirichenko et al., ICLR 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.02937).

Consistency under augmentation in forgery detection: CORE (Ni et al., CVPR Workshops 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.02749) and FreqDebias (Kashiani et al., CVPR 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.22412: 'spectral bias', frequency mixup plus consistency terms; same first author as the morph-detection consistency paper). A caution for the second arm of 5.3, since our own consistency loss gave no gain.

Data-alignment line of generated-image detection, absent from the analysis's list of remedies (probably covered by sibling analyses): B-Free (Guillaro et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.17671), Aligned Datasets (Rajan et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.11835), Fake or JPEG? (Grommelt et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.17608), Stay-Positive (Rajan and Lee, https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.07778). Note the label: there a reconstruction of a real image is 'fake'; under our rule it is genuine. Only ED4 and the rebalanced protocol label processed real material as real.

NTIRE 2026 Robust Deepfake Detection Challenge, seen through one entry (Le-Phan et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.25889, 4th of 94 teams): the field now runs a challenge on blur and heavy compression; the entry is an ensemble, so nothing transfers.

Recalled, not verified (search budget exhausted): DRCT (Chen et al., ICML 2024, reconstructions of real images as hard samples labelled fake); IDSwapMAD (Banas et al., EURASIP J. Inf. Secur. 2026, in our planning record); a null-space method for CLIP features in generated-image detection ('NS-Net', 2025); patch-relation methods before pairwise self-consistency (Chen et al., AAAI 2021); morph source-attribution work (Colbois thesis, Idiap 2025).

references_wrong_or_unverifiable: Pasquini et al., Applied Sciences 13(2):816, 2023 (https://www.mdpi.com/2076-3417/13/2/816): could not be opened (HTTP 403 twice); title, authors and content not verified by me. It is a named source of idea 5.

Liu et al., 'Detecting Generated Images by Real Images' (LNP), ECCV 2022: exists, but is described as 'real-only training' (family G and source of idea 2). The authors' code trains the final classifier on real and fake folders with the CNNDetection code; only the noise extractor is tied to real images. Not a one-class method.

Karras et al. 2019 (arXiv 1812.04948), Table 2: misread. 90% mixing is best with 1 and 2 codes (4.40, 5.11); with 3 and 4 codes 100% is best (6.63, 8.40). The analysis says 90% was best 'when several codes are mixed'.

Grommelt et al. (arXiv 2403.17608), Table 4: the +11.06 / +11.74 gains come from JPEG-96-only training AND a size constraint together (Section 4.2), not from 'training only on quality-96 images'. No ablation separates the two; the JPEG-only effect is Table 3.

Guillaro et al., B-Free (arXiv 2412.17671), Figure 2: not 'the same generated images' paired with different real sets. The fakes of the two rows are generated from different source sets (RAISE, COCO) and tested against reals of their own set; what is constant is detector and generator. The paper calls the detectors 'ViT-based'.

Colbois and Marcel, IJCB 2024 (arXiv 2410.16802), Table 7: quoted selectively. The DNADet one-class row is 0.87 / 0.82 / 0.48% on FRGC-based morphs and 27.10 / 29.10 / 32.80% on FFHQ-based morphs; only the first half is quoted.

Agustsson et al. (arXiv 1711.01970): '(strong) outliers in 100 dimensions' joins two passages (appendix phrase for large dimension; the 100-dimension statement in Section 2 reads 'dramatically different, having almost no common support'). ICLR 2019 venue not visible on any page I opened.

Chen et al., Dual Data Alignment (arXiv 2505.14359): the 93% is in the running text and is for the SAFE detector, not Figures 4 and 5; DDA-COCO is described in the text as five subsets (a results table shows six columns), the analysis says six autoencoders.
Kynkaanniemi et al. (arXiv 1904.06991): the 2.4% of 500k paths is in the text of Section 5.1; Figure 9 only shows four example paths.

Zhang, Ramachandra, Raja, Busch (arXiv 2501.09817): content confirmed, but the CVPR Workshops 2024 venue is not shown on the arXiv page (the CVF site refused the fetch); the paper does not say which generator or inversion made the reconstructed genuine images, so 'no radius control' should read 'no generation detail given'.

Venue not confirmed on any opened page (not doubted): Albright and McCloskey (CVPR Workshops 2019), DNA-Det (AAAI 2022), Gragnaniello et al. (ICME 2021; arXiv comments say only 'conference'), and the entries the analysis itself marks 'venue from memory' apart from Rajan et al. (ICLR 2025, confirmed on the authors' code page), B-Free (CVPR 2025, confirmed on the project page) and Dual Data Alignment (NeurIPS 2025 spotlight, confirmed).

R-FLoRA (arXiv 2604.17321): listed by the analysis as 'seen in search results only'; I opened it. It exists, single author Raghavendra Ramachandra, accepted at IEEE TIFS; it can move to the verified list.

33 of the 71 entries in the analysis's verified list were not opened by me; no statement is made on them. My own web search budget ran out after one search, so no fresh searches for prior use in morph detection could be run.
claims_corrected: '0.58 to 0.63 is the expected outcome of a correct control, not a lack of power' is too strong. The measured intervals are 0.615 [0.584, 0.645], 0.632 [0.603, 0.661], 0.617 [0.587, 0.648], 0.583 [0.551, 0.616]; three of four exclude 0.5. It is a small real remainder of unknown cause.

'Our 0.89 to 0.94 is a truncation reading' is an inference, not a fact. It is the leading explanation; our record also says truncated renders differ in simple image properties at 0.96, so 'truncation' may equal 'simple image properties'.

Step 0 of idea 1 does not bound image detectors. 'No image detector can beat the best test on the exact code' is true, but a logistic fit on a few summaries of 423 codes is a lower bound on what the code carries, not the best test. A low result would not justify 'print the limit and stop'. The analyst also expects a high result and declares a high result non-decisive.

The Gaussian argument is about distributions; our spread-matched control is built pair by pair, shares a contributor with its morph and matches one Euclidean radius. In a non-isotropic space equal radius does not give equal distributions. This is a sixth candidate cause for the remainder, beside the analyst's five.

Section 4 treats published GAN cells as plain midpoints. MIPGAN optimises the code after averaging (our MIPGAN one-person controls record 150 optimisation steps with identity and perceptual losses), so the radius must be measured on those cells, not assumed.

The 'wrong radius' argument is applied only to StyleGAN. MorDIFF mixes its semantic code by a straight average and its noise code by spherical interpolation (verified, arXiv 2302.01843). Our 0.945 to 1.000 on diffusion-autoencoder morphs has no radius-matched control. Our identity-shrinkage triage found only 0.688 on that contrast with a re-encoded statistic, so radius is probably not the whole story, but the exact-code check is missing.

Idea 4: the readers are not single-mechanism instruments. The ProGAN-trained classifier and NPR were trained against LSUN real images that were WEBP-compressed and stored as PNG; detectors trained on them learned 'WEBP = real' (Rajan and Lee, Section 3.1, cited by the analysis itself). Wang et al.'s classifier also used blur and JPEG augmentation.

Idea 4: 'an up-sampling reader on landmark cells: none found' overlooks older processing-history readers applied to landmark morphs (Makrushin et al. VISAPP 2017, Benford features of quantised DCT coefficients; Neubert, image degradation analysis; Hildebrandt et al. IWBF 2017, StirTrace impact simulation of processing steps), as listed in the survey arXiv 2011.02045, Table III. Verified through the survey's bibliography only.

Idea 5: 'fine-layer content is discarded by construction' is wrong for e4e. In the code one base code from the coarsest feature map is copied to all 18 layers and each layer adds a small, penalised offset. The coarse and middle codes are mostly the base code, which sees the whole image. The encoder's own transform also resizes every input to 256 x 256.

Idea 5 contradicts our own measurement: the diffusion autoencoder's semantic code (also a 512-number encoder code) moved completely with storage history in the identity-shrinkage triage (control AUC 0.000 [0.000, 0.000]); CLIP failed too.

Idea 5: the pass mark 0.75 (two-person morph against own warped halves) lies inside the softness floor (Laplacian variance alone 0.76 at 512 px, 0.87 at 224 px) and above the exact-shape ceiling (0.725 [0.689, 0.758]; 0.687 for warped half against morph). A pass could not be told from softness.

Idea 2 as a training arm contradicts the ladder: by its own declaration the head cannot separate a two-person morph from a radius-matched one-person render and it flags one-person renders. It can only be an audit row.

Idea 3: under the policy 're-synthesised is inadmissible' the generator rows are reached by reading the generator, which is on the brief's own list of cues; and our reconstructions come from the same generator families as the test cells, which published protocols do not train on. Without a leave-one-generator-out result the rows read as trained on the test generator.

Section 6 item 1 ('StyleGAN3 was designed without aliasing'): the NVIDIA StyleGAN3 detection page reports AUC 0.92 to 0.99 for seven detectors on StyleGAN3 faces, including one trained only on ProGAN (0.92). The generator is still readable on our StyleGAN3 ladders.
Minor: Ren et al. is 16 methods in 23 pretrained variants; ZED's 90.0% average AUC is 0.6 points above the best reference (89.4); the Zhu et al. FID numbers are in the text of Section 3, not a table.

ideas.name: Radius-crossed generator ladder: remove averageness by design, measure what is left
ideas.one_line: Sound design, but its step 0 bounds nothing and its likely outcome is an absence result; start with a zero-GPU re-read of stored codes and extend the radius question to the diffusion-autoencoder ladder.
ideas.closest_prior_work_in_morph_detection: Zhang, Ramachandra, Raja, Busch, arXiv 2501.09817 (reconstructed genuine images added to sets with GAN morphs; no generation detail, no radius control). Our own spread-matched render (StyleGAN3 control pools, experiment A37) already goes further than any published control I know. No radius-crossed design found; limit: I could run no new search, so this rests on the analyst's three searches and the planning record.
ideas.likeliest_confound: Softness and other simple image properties, riding on a radius mismatch that one scalar per code does not remove (our record: truncated renders differ from plain renders in simple image properties at 0.96). For the new arm (midpoint pushed back to full radius) also generator artefacts off the well-rendered region, which would be specific to the 'mixed' class. Controls: match radius per layer around the mean of the set's own codes; report the seven simple statistics on every contrast as the floor; keep the arm built from mapping-network samples (no inversion); folds grouped by both contributors.
ideas.revised_first_test: (1) One hour, CPU, no render: on the 423 StyleGAN3 pairs and 64 GAN blocks compute the AUC of the 16 per-layer radii alone (set-mean centre) for morph against one-identity render, and the probe's remainder on morph against spread-matched render after regressing out the per-layer radii, folds by both contributors. If radius alone is within 0.05 of the probe (0.89 to 0.94) and the remainder's interval includes 0.5: print 'no trace beyond radius at n = 423' and stop. (2) Minutes: the same radius read on the generating semantic codes of the diffusion-autoencoder ladder (two-person morph, same-person mix, one-photo reconstruction at 20 steps). If radius alone reaches 0.90, reword 'frozen features read the mixing step' to 'read averageness' and add a radius-matched one-photo reconstruction (decode only) to tonight's generation run. (3) Only if a remainder survives (1): render the four arms from 4 x 2,000 mapping-network samples; pass 0.70 in both radius strata, kill 0.60 with the radius positive control at 0.90 or more.
ideas.reason: Measured remainder beyond radius is small (0.58 to 0.63; same-person mix to two-person morph 0.65), so the realistic result is a well-powered absence statement for the audit, not a table number. A pass would read 'two codes were mixed', which is also true of a same-person mix, so it would not give the two-person against same-person contrast the ladder demands. The analysis's Gaussian argument is correct algebra and the sources check out (Agustsson et al.; Zhu et al.; Wulff and Torralba).

ideas.name: Truncation-dose training: a pseudo-morph with no morph and no partner
ideas.one_line: Keep as a one-hour audit row among the morph-free references; drop the training arm and the 'mixing-equivalent truncation' unit.
ideas.closest_prior_work_in_morph_detection: SelfMAD (arXiv 2504.05504; pseudo-morphs by pixel self-blending) and the quality-as-signal line: Fu and Damer, IET Biometrics (arXiv 2208.05864; MagFace and CNNNIQA as unsupervised morph signal) and 'When Morphs Look Better' (arXiv 2611.00074, in our planning record). None trains on latent truncation. Limit: no new search could be run.
ideas.likeliest_confound: Softness and backdrop. Truncation toward the generator's mean code also averages background, pose and lighting and changes sharpness; our record says truncated renders are separable by simple image properties at 0.96 and 'must not be read as typicality'. Controls: fit the seven simple statistics on the same training contrast and test them on the same morph contrast (floor trained the same way); repeat with everything outside the face box blanked in one constant colour in both classes.
ideas.revised_first_test: First read the generation record of the truncated pools (centre, layers, base codes). Fit the frozen-feature probe on psi = 0.7 renders against plain renders, folds by person, and report on held-out persons: (a) morph against one-identity render, pass at least 0.85 and within 0.05 of the morph-trained probe, kill below 0.75; (b) the simple-statistics floor trained and tested the same way; if within 0.03 of the probe, the row is worded 'simple image properties', not 'averageness'; (c) morph against spread-matched render, must be at most 0.60. Under an hour on cached features.
ideas.reason: Cheap, all images exist, and it shows constructively that a head which never saw a morph or a second person detects StyleGAN3 morphs. As a training arm it contradicts the ladder (declared unable to tell a two-person morph from a radius-matched one-person render; flags one-person renders) and, as the analysis admits, cannot reach the published generator rows. One of its three source techniques (LNP as 'real-only training') is mischaracterised; the idea does not depend on it.

ideas.name: A declared 're-synthesised' output built by the aligned-pair recipe
ideas.one_line: The only idea that touches the generator rows, but it reaches them by reading the generator; test cross-generator transfer and the history control on cached features before any training, and only after the author's class ruling.
ideas.closest_prior_work_in_morph_detection: Zhang, Ramachandra, Raja, Busch, arXiv 2501.09817 (reconstructions inside the genuine class; print-scan and compression applied to both classes) and multi-class outputs over morph tools (Zhang, Jia, Lyu, Li, arXiv 2210.15510). In the source field the three-way split exists and was missed by the analysis: Mandelli, Bestagini, Tubaro, arXiv 2407.10736 (pristine, laundered, fully synthetic). A three-way morph detector with a same-photo aligned middle class was not found (limit: no new search).
ideas.likeliest_confound: Storage history and frame: the reconstruction is a 1024-pixel render brought to our frame, the photo is a camera file of another size, and our record says the 0.98 step 'contains frame, background and resolution changes besides the generator'. For the morph output on diffusion morphs, sharpness: Laplacian variance alone gives 0.966 at 100 steps. Controls: both members of a pair through one identical path from the shared 512 frame; history-matched and stored-small photos in the genuine class at test with shift at most 0.3 SD on both outputs; train the morph output only on the matched 20-step contrast.
ideas.revised_first_test: No training of the main network. A three-way linear probe on the cached features, folds by person, half a day: (1) photo against history-matched copy on both outputs, shift at most 0.3 SD and flag rate at most 10% at the 5% threshold; (2) leave one generator out: fit the middle output on StyleGAN3 reconstructions, test on diffusion-autoencoder reconstructions and on the MIPGAN one-person controls, and the reverse. Pass: at least 0.90 across generators with (1) passing. Kill: below 0.75 across generators or (1) failing; then the output reads one pipeline and the class cannot be offered.
ideas.reason: Generator fingerprint is on the brief's cue list, so this is a declared cue, not claim (b). The morph output on GAN morphs would rest on contrasts measured at 0.65 to 0.78. Reconstructions come from the test cells' generator families, so published-row comparisons need a leave-one-generator-out result; the source field's own transfer number is poor (9.59% and 25.87%, Rajan et al., limitations, confirmed). Adds a head and two data arms to the main network with three days left.

ideas.name: Morph-free mechanism readers from the GAN field as independent instruments
ideas.one_line: Narrow to one reader (the ProGAN-trained classifier) and the one new control (GAN morph against one-person reconstruction on the published cells); the readers are mixed-cue, not single-mechanism.
ideas.closest_prior_work_in_morph_detection: Colbois and Marcel, BIOSIG 2022 (arXiv 2209.00404; the ProGAN-trained classifier unchanged on three GAN morph sets, EER 0.00 / 0.56 / 0.00%, Table 2, confirmed) and IJCB 2024 (arXiv 2410.16802; DNADet features with a probe or one-class model). Processing-history readers on landmark morphs go back to Makrushin et al. VISAPP 2017 (Benford features of DCT coefficients), Neubert (image degradation) and Hildebrandt et al. IWBF 2017 (StirTrace), as listed in the survey arXiv 2011.02045, Table III. Only the matched ladder and the one-person control are new.
ideas.likeliest_confound: Our own aligner and the file attribute. NPR reads differences inside 2 x 2 pixel blocks; any interpolation leaves that pattern, and our aligner's resize factor depends on source file size, which differs by class in all 17 cells. Both readers were also trained against WEBP-compressed LSUN reals (Rajan and Lee, Section 3.1). Control: score native files through the reader's own no-resize, no-crop path; require the photo against history-matched copy contrast on the same path; print no mechanism word unless both agree.
ideas.revised_first_test: Two hours, the released classifier of Wang et al. only: (1) published GAN cells, camera photo against morph, must reproduce Colbois and Marcel's Table 2 within one point of EER; (2) same cells, one-person control (MIPGAN one-person controls, one-photo reconstructions) against morph, expected at most 0.60; (3) photo against history-matched copy. Useful if (1) reproduces and (2) is at most 0.60. NPR and DNA-Det only with time left, on native files, without mechanism claims; the NPR page states no licence.
ideas.reason: We already hold stronger evidence of the same kind (a file attribute separates all 17 cells; no released detector separates a StyleGAN3 morph from a one-person render). An outside witness adds one quotable sentence, not a new fact. NPR weights are confirmed public (NPR.pth, model_epoch_last_3090.pth).

ideas.name: Inversion-encoder bottleneck: read identity typicality where storage history cannot reach
ideas.one_line: Its shortcut-free argument is contradicted by the encoder's design and by our own measurements, and its pass mark sits inside the softness floor and above the shape ceiling.
ideas.closest_prior_work_in_morph_detection: MorDeephy (Medvedev, Shadmand, Goncalves, arXiv 2208.03110; single-image detection tied to face recognition), quality and typicality scores (Fu and Damer, arXiv 2208.05864; arXiv 2611.00074) and our own identity-shrinkage triage (experiment ID0). No detector that reads the radius of an inversion code was found (limit: no new search; Pasquini et al., one named source, could not be opened).
ideas.likeliest_confound: Softness. e4e copies one base code from the coarsest feature map to all 18 layers and adds small penalised offsets, so the coarse and middle codes see the whole image; its transform resizes every input to 256 x 256. Laplacian variance alone already gives 0.76 to 0.87 on the pass contrast. Control: photo blended with its own mirror against the warped half must stay at or below 0.60; the claim may be carried only by two-person against same-person morph as excess over Laplacian variance on the same pairs.
ideas.revised_first_test: Not recommended. If run anyway (two hours): only two-person against same-person morph on the landmark ladder, with the Laplacian-variance floor on the same pairs and the photo against history-matched copy shift; continue only if the excess over the floor has an interval above zero and the shift is at most 0.3 SD. Expected to fail.
ideas.reason: The nearest measured analogue, the diffusion autoencoder's semantic code, moved completely with storage history (control AUC 0.000). Exact landmark shapes give only 0.725 [0.689, 0.758] for photo against morph and 0.687 for warped half against morph, so a 0.75 pass would have to come from texture, which is the softness cue. A component that cannot reach the published rows and whose control is expected to fail is not worth a slot in three days.

missed_by_the_analyst: Mandelli, Bestagini, Tubaro. When Synthetic Traces Hide Real Content: Analysis of Stable Diffusion Image Laundering. arXiv 2407.10736, 2024. https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.10736 . A real image passed through a generator's autoencoder is called synthetic; a two-stage detector separates pristine, laundered and fully synthetic images. Closest field precedent for our 're-synthesised' class and idea 3.

NVIDIA with the SemaFor teams. StyleGAN3 Synthetic Image Detection. https://github.com/NVlabs/stylegan3-detector . Seven detectors on StyleGAN3 faces, with a resize-and-JPEG variant; AUC 0.92 to 0.99, including a detector trained only on ProGAN (0.92). The generator trace is still readable on StyleGAN3. Nothing per truncation level.

Yang, Li, Qi, Lyu. Exposing GAN-synthesized Faces Using Landmark Locations. arXiv 1904.00167, 2019. https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.00167 . Landmark positions alone separate generated from real faces: the field's version of our shape-typicality test. With Guo et al., irregular pupil shapes (https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.00162) and Hu, Li, Lyu, corneal highlights (https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.11924) this is a whole family (physical and anatomical consistency) absent from the analysis's map.

Zheng et al. NoiseDiffusion: Correcting Noise for Image Interpolation with Diffusion Models beyond Spherical Linear Interpolation. ICLR 2024, arXiv 2403.08840. https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.08840 . The diffusion counterpart of Agustsson et al.; together with the MorDIFF recipe (straight average of the semantic code, spherical interpolation of the noise code; https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.01843) it carries the 'wrong radius' question to diffusion-autoencoder morphs.

Mareen et al. TGIF: Text-Guided Inpainting Forgery Dataset. IEEE WIFS 2024, arXiv 2407.11566. https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.11566 . Spliced against fully regenerated images; generated-image detectors flag the regenerated ones without saying what changed, and fail under stronger compression.

Pal et al. Semi-Truths. NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks, arXiv 2411.07472. https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.07472 . Real images with graded edits; detectors respond unevenly to the degree of edit. The field's dose benchmark, analogue of our graded-mixing rungs.

Karageorgiou et al. Any-Resolution AI-Generated Image Detection by Spectral Learning (SPAI). CVPR 2025, arXiv 2411.19417. https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.19417 . Real-only spectral model, generated images as out of distribution; belongs in the one-class family and would formalise our softness cue.

Li et al. Is Artificial Intelligence Generated Image Detection a Solved Problem? (AIGIBench). NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks, arXiv 2505.12335. https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.12335 . Eleven detectors under degradation and test-time preprocessing; augmentation and preprocessing give limited or inconsistent gains.
Konstantinidou, Koutlis, Papadopoulos. TextureCrop. arXiv 2407.15500. https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.15500 . Cropping textured regions instead of resizing or centre cropping; same line as SAFE.

Older forensic readers in morph detection, listed in Venkatesh, Ramachandra, Raja, Busch, Face Morphing Attack Generation and Detection: A Comprehensive Survey, arXiv 2011.02045, Table III (https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.02045): Makrushin et al., VISAPP 2017 (Benford features of quantised DCT coefficients); Neubert, International Workshop on Digital Watermarking (image degradation analysis); Hildebrandt et al., IWBF 2017 (StirTrace impact simulation of processing steps). Verified through the survey's bibliography only. They are prior art for processing-history readers on morphs and for testing morph detectors under processing steps.

Medvedev, Shadmand, Goncalves. MorDeephy: Face Morphing Detection Via Fused Classification. arXiv 2208.03110. https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.03110 . Single-image morph detection tied to a face-recognition task; nearest morph detection work to 'read identity from one image'.

Recalled, not verified (search budget exhausted or page refused): Mundra, Porcile, Mohanty, Farid, GAN-generated profile photos from compact embeddings, CVPR Workshops 2023 (fixed StyleGAN face alignment as a cue); Nightingale and Farid, PNAS 2022 (synthetic faces and averageness); Spreeuwers et al. 2022, practical evaluation of morph detection methods; Banerjee and Ross, single-image demorphing, IJCB 2022; the University of Maryland GAN-Scanner inversion-based detector named on the NVIDIA page.

references_wrong_or_unverifiable: [24] Huang et al., Test-Time Adaptation for Robust Face Anti-Spoofing, BMVC 2023: the address given in the analysis (bmvc2022.mpi-inf.mpg.de/BMVC2023/379) redirects twice and ends in HTTP 404; not verified.

Not opened by me (none carries an idea): [6], [8], [9], [10], [11], [13], [14], [43], [48].

No invented reference and no wrong table number found: 46 of the 48 opened references exist with the stated authors and say what the analysis claims (full-text check for [4], [7], [12], [15], [16], [17], [22], [23], [25], [27], [28], [29], [30], [36], [37], [41], [44], [45], [47], [52], [56], [59]).
claims_corrected: PatchNet ablation (basis of idea 3): the analysis says 6.25% against 1.88% ACER with 'two changes tested together'. Table 4 of the paper also has the single-change rows: binary classes with patch input 3.54%, fine classes with resized input 5.63%. On resized whole faces (our input regime) naming the classes gives only 6.25 to 5.63. The cleaner evidence, not cited, is Table 7 (cross-domain): coarse classes 10.24 / 15.67 / 21.65 / 16.26% HTER against 7.10 / 11.33 / 14.6 / 11.82 with fine classes.

GD-FAS (basis of idea 2): the quoted ECE numbers are right but selective. The same Table 2 lists FLIP-MCL, which has no threshold alignment, at 3.94 / 1.45 / 2.62 / 5.45 against GD-FAS 3.39 / 1.82 / 2.37 / 2.86. The paper's own ablation (Table 3) shows that adding the group-wise term to the orthogonal decomposition makes ECE worse on all four splits (1.60 / 1.00 / 1.48 / 2.38 to 3.39 / 1.82 / 2.37 / 2.86); the authors state that the group term 'primarily focuses on improving generalization'. Table 1 is captioned 'Best results considered across epochs'. So the paper supports measuring the offset, not the claim that group reweighting aligns it.

One-sided cue map, Feng et al. (basis of idea 4): attacks are not left without any push. The method has a triplet loss on intermediate features and an auxiliary classifier fed with the image plus the cue map; without the classifier ACER is 1.7% against 0.4% (Table 5). 'An all-one target was worse' rests on one pair of rows (1.7 against 0.4% ACER, OULU-NPU protocol 1, intra-data-set).

IADG asymmetry: the support is 8.86 against 10.69% HTER on one split (Table 5) and is not monotone (ratio 1:0.1 gives 9.86). The follow-up paper of the same first author (Table 1 of the test-time paper) lists IADG at 11.45 / 11.04 / 8.45 / 12.74 instead of 8.86 / 10.62 / 5.41 / 8.70.

Voice anti-spoofing study: 'EER above 50% when the association is inverted' holds for MP3 and noise with the simple model and for noise with the neural model; for the neural model MP3 inversion gives about 36% and loudness and mu-law change little. The effect depends on intervention and model.

Our own record is mis-cited: the earlier consistency loss (experiment A49) was a full run (four arms, five seeds, 20.5 H100-hours) with no gain (+0.0029 [-0.0049, +0.0106]); the '16 to 90 pairs' belong to the first twin-trained heads (T0). The prior evidence against a consistency loss is therefore not an underpowered trial; what it lacked is interventional pairs.

Registered controls ignored by the proposed tests: (a) idea 4 puts its kill mark on FaceMorpher, which CONSOLIDATED_v2 section 3 declares descriptive only (the OpenCV-style engine and the Poisson set decide); (b) idea 4 uses a raw map correlation of 0.2 where the registered control is the correlation after template removal plus the pair-swap test; (c) ideas 1, 2 and 4 use R2w against R4, but R2w is warped to a same-person mean shape, so its warp is smaller than that of R4, and the record holds that warp size alone predicted same-person against two-person at AUC 0.81 pooled and 0.92 on FERET. The warp-matched negatives are the rung R2w4 registered tonight (AR1 prereg, amendment 4) and the zero-field images and warped halves of the alpha-field set.

Idea 3, 'no work with a single-subject or several genuine classes found': the repository's own class-definition note lists five papers of one group (MorDeephy, arXiv 2208.03110, and follow-ups) that train a binary detector with same-person morphs labelled genuine; I confirmed the MorDeephy text ('we consider selfmorphs as bona fide samples'). Its own ablation is mixed.

Idea 1, style line: the field's source for 'style = feature statistics' applies it in shallow layers; at the last block results fall below the baseline (MixStyle, Table 3: PACS 79.5 to 75.6; re-identification mAP 19.3 to 10.2) because statistics there carry the label. SSAN itself states that style holds liveness-related information and does not remove it. Idea 1 standardises last-layer tokens.

Idea 1, step B cannot work as written: a linear patch head on per-image centred tokens has the same mean in every image and cannot fit the constant target of a uniform morph; with top-tenth pooling its score is about 1.75 times the spread of patch scores, a second-order statistic of the kind IADG treats as style. Variant b (swap statistics within a class) cannot break a class-linked shortcut, which is the case the analysis itself describes for morph benchmarks.

ideas.name: History as style: remove per-image token statistics before the head
ideas.one_line: Standardise each token channel over the face-hull patches of one image so that uniform storage history cannot reach the head; test the premise in one hour before anything else.
ideas.closest_prior_work_in_morph_detection: Not token statistics, but the same move in the spectrum: SRL-MAD (Paulo, Proença, Neves, IWBF 2026, arXiv 2603.15050) and FD-MAD (same authors, arXiv 2601.20656) subtract from each image's log-spectrum the power-law trend fitted to that same image ('obtained per-image'), which removes the global spectral slope; neither tests benign processing of genuine images. Kashiani et al., IJCB 2023 (arXiv 2308.10392) transfer image styles. Token-statistic removal in morph detection: none known; I could not re-run the search (search budget exhausted).
ideas.likeliest_confound: Two. (1) Warp size: R2w has a same-person warp, R4 a two-person warp; local warp traces are not uniform, survive standardisation and are untouched by history, so both pass marks can be met on warp alone. Control: R2w4 or the zero-field image against the morph of the same pair. (2) Softness: averaging two faces halves fine detail almost everywhere (0.52 Laplacian ratio), so the blending trace is largely uniform too, and what survives a per-image shift and rescale is of the same kind for a blur and for an average. Control: softened warp-matched negatives against R4, read as excess over the Laplacian-variance AUC of that contrast, plus R3 and R3m against R4.
ideas.revised_first_test: Step A' (one hour, cached DINOv3 hull tokens): measure two paired changes the same way: history (FRLL photo to its history-matched frame; ladder host to its softened copy, both registered strengths) and blending (zero-field image to the uniform-0.5 morph of the same pair, identical warp). Report the share of the token change explained by a per-image, per-channel shift and rescale. Premise holds if the share is at least 0.8 for history on both pools and at least 0.2 lower for blending. KILL if the shares differ by less than 0.2. Step B (half a day, only after A'): a small non-linear patch scorer trained through top-tenth pooling with image labels, next to the identical scorer on raw tokens; decide on the OpenCV-style engine and the Poisson set. PASS: at most 10% of history-matched FRLL photos flagged at the 5% threshold; R2w4 against R4 at least 0.90; softened warped halves against R4 at least 0.05 above the Laplacian-variance AUC of that contrast; R3 against R4 not more than 0.02 below the raw-token scorer. KILL: softened contrast within 0.05 of its Laplacian floor, or more than 10% flagged.
ideas.reason: Cheap and falsifiable in an hour, and the premise measurement is informative either way. But the guarantee holds only for frozen tokens (a LoRA fit can write a global property into the spatial pattern), the field's evidence is for shallow layers and reports that last-layer statistics carry the label, the linear head of the proposed step B is structurally unable to work, and by design the method discards the strongest landmark cue. Variant b does not address a class-linked shortcut.

ideas.name: One-threshold training: align the genuine side only, and align the offset
ideas.one_line: Keep the per-environment fixed-threshold read-out without any test; test the genuine-only loss terms on a history strength that was not in training, with a non-linear head, before a LoRA arm.
ideas.closest_prior_work_in_morph_detection: Kashiani et al., IJCB 2023 (arXiv 2308.10392): symmetric consistency between a training image and its augmented view, with domain discriminators. Evaluation side only: NIST FATE MORPH per-pool false detections (our record) and Marriott, NIST IFPC 2025 (fixed threshold under compression, retraining helps partly). No genuine-only or offset alignment known in morph detection (planning record section 11 holds an earlier negative search; I could not repeat it). Outside morph detection the parts are published: SSDG (arXiv 2004.14043), an asymmetric invariant-risk method with one radius shared across domains (Lin et al., arXiv 2511.14157), risk equalisation with a real-only contrastive term (Cai et al., IJCV 2024, arXiv 2409.03501), equal false-positive rate at one threshold (Xu et al., CVPR 2021, arXiv 2106.05519).
ideas.likeliest_confound: Storage history seen in training: the softened copies use the two registered strengths, which are the family medians of FRLL-Morphs AMSL and MAD22 FaceMorpher, and the FRLL test frames are built by the same path at family medians, so a head can learn two strengths by heart and pass. Control: leave one strength out, in both directions. Second: capture detail between photo pools moves the genuine level and the offset term cannot align an unseen pool. Control: hold one pool out with at least three genuine pools in training, and check that morphs made from a genuine-only pool do not score lower. Third: softness is also the real morph trace, so the terms can pass by discarding it. Control: bound the rise of MACER at the fixed threshold and read softened warp-matched negatives against R4.
ideas.revised_first_test: One day, CPU, cached pooled CLIP ViT-L/14 and DINOv3 features, two-layer head (so the loss is not the known linear projection), three fixed seeds with the mean reported. Heads on identical images: (1) data only, with softened genuine copies of ONE strength as negatives; (2) plus the per-host term; (3) plus the offset term; warp negatives are R2w4 or zero-field images. Threshold at 5% of native training-pool photos. Read BPCER on the LEFT-OUT strength (held-out hosts), on FRLL history-matched frames per family and on FRLL native photos; MACER on FRLL two-person morphs at the same threshold; repeat with the strengths exchanged. PASS: on the left-out strength BPCER at most 10% and at most half that of head 1 in both directions, with MACER not more than 2 points above head 1. If head 1 is already at or below 10%, stop: the data arm suffices. KILL: no halving on the left-out strength. Only after a pass: one LoRA arm next to the planned data arm.
ideas.reason: It fits the measured failure and plugs into the paper's chain, and its read-out is needed anyway. But the data-only route already reaches 4 to 8% flagged shrunk photos, a consistency loss already failed in a full run (experiment A49), and the cited source for offset alignment does not show that the group term improves calibration. The loss terms are a recombination of published parts with weak evidence of gain.

ideas.name: Name the nuisance: a classifier over ladder rungs with two-person morph as one class
ideas.one_line: Drop the softmax-over-rungs head as a detector design; keep the rungs as negatives and, at most, a multinomial probe as a diagnostic.
ideas.closest_prior_work_in_morph_detection: MorDeephy (Medvedev, Shadmand, Gonçalves, arXiv 2208.03110) and four follow-ups of the same group (listed in 14_CLASS_DEFINITIONS.md): same-person morphs labelled genuine in a binary detector, to keep the detector off blending artefacts; their own ablation is mixed. Opposite labelling: Kashiani et al., IJCB 2023 and SelfMAD, FG 2025. Reconstructed genuine images: Zhang et al., arXiv 2501.09817. Attack-side multi-class: Zhang, Jia, Lyu, Li, arXiv 2210.15510. Only the softmax over named rungs is new.
ideas.likeliest_confound: Warp size and the session match of the two contributors. Same-person photo pairs often share session, backdrop, light and clothing, and their landmark shapes differ less; warp size alone gave AUC 0.81 and 0.92 for same-person against two-person, and a head that never saw a same-person morph reaches 0.853 / 0.830 on the large pool but 0.948 / 0.932 on FRLL. Host matching equalises the host, not the partner. Control: read the contrast inside thirds of landmark displacement, blank everything outside the face hull, and print the AUC of landmark displacement alone and of Laplacian variance alone.
ideas.revised_first_test: Only if the idea is taken up again (half a day, CPU, cached features): binary head and six-way head on identical images. PASS: within displacement thirds and with the surround blanked, same-person against two-person exceeds the better of the two single-cue AUCs (landmark displacement, Laplacian variance) by at least 0.05 on both engines, and the six-way head beats the binary head by at least 0.02 there. KILL: either fails.
ideas.reason: The source evidence is weaker than quoted (fine classes on resized faces: 6.25 to 5.63%). The claim that a binary head has nowhere to put softness evidence fails once softened genuine copies are negatives, which the baseline already has. The defining contrast is where our signal is weakest and most confounded (0.65 on GAN ladders; warp size and session on landmark ladders), the class list awaits the author, and a softmax score at a fixed threshold depends on training class shares.

ideas.name: One-sided zero map: genuine constructions regress to zero, morphs get no template
ideas.one_line: Add it as a sixth arm of the registered ablation of the alpha-field probe (AF0), with warp-matched and single-identity averaged zero targets and the registered template and pair-swap controls.
ideas.closest_prior_work_in_morph_detection: PW-MAD (Damer et al., ISVC 2021, arXiv 2108.10291): two-sided constant maps. One-class detectors: SPL-MAD (arXiv 2208.05787), MAD-DDPM (arXiv 2306.15733), SRL-MAD (arXiv 2603.15050). The exact loss form exists outside morph detection: FCDD (Liznerski et al., ICLR 2021, arXiv 2007.01760), a map pulled to zero on normal images and pushed up on anomalous ones with image labels only; its authors report such maps reading spurious features. A one-sided map in morph detection: none known; search not repeatable.
ideas.likeliest_confound: Type of softness plus an anatomy pattern. Softness from shrink-and-enlarge and softness from averaging differ in the spectrum, so with softened copies as the only soft zero targets the head can call the first zero and the second energy, and a global flag satisfies both the zero targets and the hinge; energy also rises on textured regions, where the true field is larger, so a raw correlation of 0.2 can be a template. Control: correlation after template removal and the pair-swap test (both registered); warped halves and zero-field images as warp-matched zero targets; mirror self-blend and same-person morph as averaged single-identity zero targets, with R3m and R3 against R4 read next to the measured-map arm.
ideas.revised_first_test: CPU after tokens, one arm added to the registered five-arm ablation: absolute-value loss to zero on photos, warped halves and their softened copies; hinge on the top-tenth map energy of a morph over its own warped half; a second variant adds R3m and R3 as zero targets. Decide on the OpenCV-style engine and the Poisson set (FaceMorpher descriptive only). PASS: correlation with the true field after template removal at least 0.2 on gradient and bump images, pair-swap lower bound above 0.10, at most 10% of softened halves flagged at the 5% threshold, morph against softened half at least 0.05 above the Laplacian-variance AUC of that contrast. KILL: template-removed correlation below 0.2, or the arm is not better than the image-label arm with halves as negatives on any registered read-out.
ideas.reason: Almost free as one more arm, but removing the positive template does not answer the round-2 objection (a global flag still fits), the proposal lacks the zero targets that separate blending from a second identity, its kill mark sits on an engine declared descriptive only, and it repairs a component that is no longer the headline.
